_doc: THE WORKER ENVELOPE (V2-831 T-27). Background work shares the host with the voice, and a host that runs out of
memory freezes the voice first: on a small host with no swap, free memory can fall to zero while errands run,
the VAD falls behind real time and the host freezes. Every number here is a RATIO of what the host measures at
run time (psutil), never an absolute for one machine, so the same file holds on a laptop, a small server or a
large one. A deployment that needs other values writes `config/resources.json` beside this file (same keys).
A new worker waits for room with NO clock (V2-867): until the floor holds, the voice's shed ends and the worker
admitted before it RUNS — one at a time on a tight host; the operator's cancel is the exit, never a deadline.
The floor is the LARGER of `admit_free_ratio` of the total and `voice_reserve_mb`: the engine's measured RSS is
284-600 MB with the voice session embedded, so 768 MB keeps its peak plus a margin free for the voice; on a 4 GB
host the ratio (~780 MB) and the reserve agree, on a 2 GB host the ratio alone (~410 MB) would not hold one voice.
`voice_lag_s` is the voice's own lag bound (T-30): over it, an event, one spoken notice and load shed.
THE SELF WATCHDOG (T-28): a thread beats the server loop; `freeze_s` without an answer, or free memory under
`pause_free_ratio`, sheds load; still so after `stuck_s` and under a supervisor (ZAELAR_SUPERVISED=1) it exits
non-zero for a restart, ended hard `exit_grace_s` later if the loop cannot shut down.
`summary_push_s` (T-31): how often the compact summary goes to ZAELAR_SUMMARY_URL, when a deployment sets one.
`browser_bg_wait_s` (pass 10): how long a background search waits for HIS turn's search in the one browser.
THE VOICE RECYCLE (V2-871): the old LiveKit worker's close is waited `recycle_close_s`, then abandoned; the new one
must register within `recycle_verify_s`, retried `recycle_attempts` times `recycle_backoff_s` apart (doubling).
Gave up, or no live worker `voice_dead_s` after a session was asked for: an alert, and under a supervisor an exit
for a restart; unsupervised a new try every `recycle_retry_s`. `boot_grace_s` is the cold start (models, browser,
the first connection; a first session measured 2.5 min to listening on a small host): degraded marks and the
audio lag inside it are the warm-up, never a degradation.
